results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks pair them with.

The three requested cards have no published list together, so I need to see what enablers exist. Next I'll check the meta, the Rogue shell, and the mill and reanimation cards in Standard.

Town Greeter is green, and Spider-Man and Bringer are black and blue, so no single existing shell fits all three. I'll look at the two closest shells, Dimir and Golgari, and search for graveyard and removal enablers.

Dimir Midrange is the most established U/B shell, but Town Greeter is green. Before choosing a direction I'll check the removal, mana and creature cards that the candidate shells would use.

Two findings change the plan: Go for the Throat and Cut Down are not legal in Standard, and Town Greeter can only be cast with green. I'll build a Golgari reanimator (black-green, with a small blue splash for Superior Spider-Man). Before submitting I'll check the deck and the odds of finding blue and the key reanimation pieces.

The deck passes the checker with no errors or warnings, and the blue splash reaches 72% by turn 5 on the play. Submitting it now.

The checker flagged Graveshifter and Bristlebud Farmer. I'll swap Graveshifter for Soulcoil Viper, which is a second reanimation enabler, and keep Bristlebud Farmer as a 5/5 body that mills.

I built a Golgari reanimator (black-green with a five-Island-equivalent blue splash for Superior Spider-Man), and it was accepted with no warnings. The plan is to survive the aggro start with cheap removal and deathtouch blockers, mill into the graveyard, then cheat Bringer of the Last Gift onto the battlefield. The main line is Vile Entomber on turn 4 to put Bringer into the graveyard, then Zombify on turn 5 to return it as a 6/6 flier without triggering the board wipe. Superior Spider-Man can copy Bringer from the graveyard as a backup.

I chose this direction over a Dimir build because Dimir cannot cast Town Greeter, and Town Greeter was one of the three cards you named. The shell is borrowed from Golgari Midrange for its mana, with a three-copy Spider-Man splash on six blue sources.

The honest odds are weak: all the cards in the win line show up together by turn 6 in only about 2% of games, and that figure does not simulate tutors. The deck also runs only two Vile Entombers and two Zombifies, so the line depends on a lot of luck. Treat it as a playable brew, not a proven list.

winLine.does: On turn 4, its ETB searches the library for Bringer of the Last Gift and puts it into the graveyard (a tutor into the yard, not a cast).
On turn 5, returns Bringer from the graveyard to the battlefield. It was not cast, so the board-wipe trigger does not fire; a 6/6 flier arrives for 4 mana.
Attacks in the air for 6 per turn while the rest of the deck handles the early pressure.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I built a green-red landfall deck with a light blue splash for Spell Snare, borrowing the Landfall list's green core and mana base. The Simic option would have used Spell Snare and Harmonizer but only one red card. The Izzet option would have dropped Harmonizer, and I didn't want to lose it. Red had the stronger support: Full Bore, Nova Hellkite's warp, and the Burst Lightning and Obliterating Bolt removal that the current field relies on.

**The plan:** Turn 4 with three lands and Llanowar Elves, warp Mightform Harmonizer for 3 and cast Full Bore for R. Full Bore gives the warped Harmonizer haste and trample, then the fourth land triggers landfall to double its power, so it attacks for 14 trample. The rest of the list is cheap landfall creatures, burn, and Nova Hellkite as the finisher.

**Odds and caveats:** The full line needs Llanowar Elves, Harmonizer and Full Bore by turn 4, and the tools put that at about 11–13% of games. Each card on its own is about 53% by turn 4 on the play. No published list runs these three cards together, so this is an untested brew. Spell Snare is only a 1-mana counter for MV2 spells, so I kept it at two copies.

Submitted as a brew: 24 lands, 36 main spells, 15-card sideboard. The check passed with no errors or warnings.

winLine.does: Turn 1-2 mana: with 3 lands plus Elves, gives 4 mana on turn 4 for warp plus Full Bore.
Warp for {2}{G} on turn 4: a 4/4 that is exiled at end of turn, so it is a haste-able attacker from the warp cost.
Cast on the warped Harmonizer for {R}: +3/+2 and, because it was warped, trample and haste (7/6 trample haste).
Play the 4th land after Full Bore resolves: landfall doubles the target's power 7 to 14, then attack for 14 trample.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
I built a blue-red Elemental deck around Sunderflock. Every creature is an Elemental, so Sunderflock's ETB wipes the opponent's non-Elementals while your board survives. Flamebraider ramps you into a 6 or 7 MV Elemental (Ice Flan, Mouth of the Storm, Eddymurk Crab, Shinestriker), which cuts Sunderflock to about 2–3 mana. Bounce Off, Into the Flood Maw, burn and Chandra handle the rest.

I chose this over two other directions. A Simic Elementals build (Galewind Moose, Wistfulness, Lumra) would have needed green ramp to reach the same costs. A Simic Ouroboroid build with Bounce Off has the most play in the results, but it has almost no Elementals, so Sunderflock would be a dead card. The blue-red mana is borrowed from Rogue, which is the only real list that plays Sunderflock; I didn't copy its creatures.

The win line is Flamebraider on turn 2, Ice Flan on turn 4, then Sunderflock on turn 5 for three mana. Its odds are low: about 24% to have both an MV 6–7 Elemental and Sunderflock by turn 6 on the play, computed before I added Shinestriker as a sixth enabler. The deck is 24 lands and passes check_deck with no warnings.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:

The three cards are a sacrifice package: Freebooter and Bagginses make Treasure, and Zealot wants fodder to sacrifice. I'll look for the sacrifice enablers and payoffs in Standard, and check the menu's black cards.

The sacrifice package has real support in black. Next I'll pull card facts for the menu's black cards and check the black archetypes' lists.

Mono-black has enough removal and bodies to support a sacrifice shell. I'll check the black sacrifice outlets and payoffs in more detail.

I have enough to choose a direction. Three options were on the table, and I'm picking the mono-black sacrifice build. Before I finalise, I'll run the checker on the 60-card list against Mardu Discard's shell, since it's the closest borrowed shell for Bloodghast.

The checker passes: 60 cards, 22 real lands plus Tarrian's Journal, and 15 sideboard cards. The Mardu source warnings don't apply to a mono-black build. Submitting now.

I built a mono-black sacrifice deck around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot. It is a brew: none of the three cards has a published list, and their own search found no real deck running all three together. The checker passed it with no errors or warnings.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three options: mono-black sacrifice, Dimir (blue-black) sacrifice-midrange, and a Mardu Discard shell. I picked mono-black because it has enough cheap removal and bodies, and it keeps the early Freebooter, Zealot and Bagginses drops consistent. The only card borrowed from the menu is Bloodghast, which recurs off landfall to keep feeding the sacrifice engine.

**The plan:** Turn 1 Freebooter, turn 2 Zealot, turn 3 Bagginses sacrificing a Freebooter or Sage for a card and a Treasure. Freebooter, Infestation Sage, Bloodghast and Experimental Confectioner supply the fodder that feeds Zealot, Bagginses and Ahriman's card draw. Heartless Act, Bitter Triumph and Murder handle threats, and Liliana, Dreadhorde General is the finisher.

**Mana:** 21 Swamp, Midgar, City of Mako and Tarrian's Journal (a sacrifice outlet that also plays as a land). That gives 23 black sources, which keeps Bloodghast's landfall working.

**Limitation:** the deck has no published results behind it, so its power level is an informed estimate, not a tested result. I'd expect it to be weakest against fast boards of small creatures and strongest once the sacrifice engine starts drawing cards. The sideboard is 15 cards aimed at the field, including Day of Black Sun against the small-creature decks.

Goblin Welder sacrifices one artifact and returns another from the graveyard, and Sewer-veillance Cam untaps a creature when it leaves the battlefield. Welder can therefore untap itself on every loop, and Legion Extruder's 2-damage ETB fires each time. I'll verify the Vintage power pieces I want before building.

Most of the power pieces are restricted to one copy in Vintage, which shapes the build. Force of Will and Force of Negation are legal at four. Next I'll check the list, the Vintage deck rules, and the opening-hand odds for the combo pieces.

The list is legal and within the Vintage rules. The checker's land warning is worth answering: the deck runs 8 lands plus 11 zero-to-one-mana accelerants, about 19 mana sources, which matches its recommended count. I'll check the three-piece odds by turn 3 before submitting.

The revised list passes with only the land-count warning, which I'll explain in the answer. Submitting now.

I built a Vintage deck around a Goblin Welder loop that deals infinite damage, and it passed the submit checker.

**Plan:** Goblin Welder sacrifices an artifact and returns another from the graveyard, and Sewer-veillance Cam untaps the Welder whenever it leaves the battlefield. So you can swap Cam and Legion Extruder back and forth with no mana cost, and each Extruder return deals 2 damage. The deck is four copies each of Welder, Cam, Extruder and Goblin Engineer. The Engineer puts an artifact into the graveyard to seed the loop. Eleven zero-to-one-mana artifacts (Moxen, Chrome Mox, Black Lotus, Lotus Petal, Mana Crypt, Sol Ring) get the pieces out on turns 1–2. Four Force of Will and four Force of Negation protect the combo, with Pyroblast and Red Elemental Blast against blue decks.

**Direction:** Three options. (a) The Welder/Cam loop on a Vintage power base, which I chose because it wins on its own with cheap pieces. (b) A Legacy-style value build with Chaos Defiler and Phyrexian Dragon Engine, which has no kill. (c) A counter-heavy shell borrowed from the field's Lurrus Control list; I folded its Force and Misstep package into (a) rather than building it separately.

**Caveats:**
- The real Legacy Sewer lists run four Urza's Saga and four Lotus Petal, which are restricted to one copy each in Vintage. I could not copy that list as built.
- Odds are modest. Each combo piece shows up about 45–49% of the time by turn 2–3 on the play, and all three together by turn 3 about 10%. The line-completion stat from the submit tool is 0.7% of games by turn 3 (tutors and cantrips not simulated).
- The checker warns about low land count. I kept 8 lands, which with the 11 mana artifacts gives about 19 mana sources, roughly what it recommends.
- I swapped out Mishra's Research Desk after the submit checker flagged it as almost never played, for Soul-Guide Lantern and Fury.
